title: The value of broadscale semi-autonomous seabed monitoring from the perspective of a marine fisheries monitoring programme
content:
Abstract
Management of the marine environment is progressively adopting an ecosystem-based approach, which necessitates an integrated strategy for monitoring. Collecting the various required data types simultaneously is often challenging, primarily because of the specific gear needed (such as grabs, trawls, and video and acoustic equipment) and discrepancies in their spatial and temporal scales. To accommodate the need for the collection of habitat data from fisheries surveys on the RV Endeavour, semi-autonomous multibeam data collection, processing, and classifying has been developed. We have tested the influence of the multibeam data, in comparison to seabed data (modelled kinetic energy and depth) gathered by other means, by the fit of negative binomial models of 32 demersal species from the western Channel. The study analysed 508 sampling stations across six habitat classes with varying depths and kinetic energy levels. We found that for the habitat class variable produced by semi-autonomous means was as valuable to the modelling of the demersal as other data sources. A semi-automated approach to broadscale habitat mapping has the potential to inform species distribution modelling required from an ecosystem-based management approach in the future.
